title: Support Ticket ↔ DM Sync Sequence
purpose: Show the bidirectional synchronization between support tickets and direct messages, including the dynamic require() circular dependency workaround
audience: Backend developers, platform maintainers, QA engineers
description: Cross-service synchronization between support tickets and direct messages. When an admin replies to a support ticket, the support service appends the reply to the ticket's JSONB conversation array and then calls MessageService.sendDirectMessage() via dynamic require() to create a DM from the admin to the user. The DM is broadcast via Socket.IO to the user's room. Conversely, when a user sends a DM to an admin, the message service detects the admin receiver, calls supportService.appendUserMessageToActiveTicket(), which appends the message to the user's active ticket and changes the ticket status from Pending back to Open.

Ticket status transitions: Pending → Open when user replies to a Pending ticket

validationRules: Admin reply requires protectAndAdmin middleware (JWT + admin role)
Admin reply text must be non-empty string
Ticket must exist and not be in Resolved status
User must have status = 'active' to send messages
businessRules: Dynamic require() at support.service.ts:71 is a circular dependency workaround — should be converted to static import
JSONB conversation array lacks relational model — no separate support_messages table for querying and indexing
No email notification sent to user when admin replies to ticket (despite SMTP being configured)
Ticket status transitions: Open → Pending (admin views) → Open (user replies) → Resolved
User cannot view their own ticket history — admin-only visibility
No SLA tracking, escalation, reassignment, or priority fields exist
securityConsiderations: Admin role required for ticket reply — enforced by protectAndMiddleware
User messages to admin are copied to ticket conversation — platform can read all messages
Dynamic require() is a runtime security concern — could potentially load unexpected modules if path manipulation occurs
No admin audit trail — actions not logged
Full conversation history stored as JSONB array with sender names
performanceConsiderations: JSONB append on large conversation arrays may become slow over time
Dynamic require() adds minimal overhead but bypasses static analysis and bundling
Each admin reply triggers DM creation — adds latency to ticket reply endpoint
No caching on support ticket queries — every page load queries the table
No email notification reduces external call overhead but reduces user experience
